P8286.notes: The project is entirely in Virginia (Pittsylvania, Campbell and Fairfax counties), not North Carolina to Maryland. The July 2006 application notice gives 16.39 miles of new loop (Pittsylvania and Campbell) plus 3.43 miles of replacement in Fairfax. The February 2006 scoping notice gave 17.2 plus 4.0 miles of loop (21.2 total) and 3.4 miles of replacement. The January 2007 EA notice gives about 16.4 miles of 42-inch pipe. The final split between Pittsylvania and Campbell counties was not found, so the 17.2 and 4.0 figures are the scoping-stage values. GEM's 19.37 mi cannot be reproduced from these notices. Loop start and end mileposts were NOT found: the EA and order are on FERC eLibrary and were not reachable. Known anchors are the Fairfax pig launcher and receiver at MP 1586.17 and Compressor Station 165 at Mainline MP 1413.0 (from the Leidy Southeast EA station table). No coordinates found.

P8281.notes: Source is the FERC environmental assessment for CP13-551. Table 1.2.1-1 gives name, counties, begin and end mileposts and length for all four loops. The four loops total 29.8 mi, matching the project. The EA says the Skillman Loop extends between existing mainline valves at MP 1776.8 and 1783.0. Leidy Line MP 0 is at Centerville Regulator Station (MP 0.11, Somerset County NJ) per the 2001 Leidy East application. Final certificate lengths may differ slightly (other sources give Pleasant Run 6.83 to 6.92 mi, Skillman 6.18 to 6.36 mi). No coordinates found. Township names (Princeton and Montgomery for Skillman; Branchburg, Readington and Clinton for Pleasant Run) came from search snippets only and are not verified, so they are left out of the place fields.

P8280.notes: From the June 2001 notice of application for CP01-389. Clinton Loop mileposts are given in descending order in the source (18.25 to 13.62). The Benton Loop runs from Columbia County (MP 33.19) to Luzerne County (MP 39.28). The six loops sum to 30.56 mi, close to the 31 mi on file. Only the application was read. The certificate (late 2001) may have changed lengths or mileposts, and not every loop may have been built. Station anchors stated: Compressor Station 520 at MP 157.52 (Lycoming), 515 at MP 68.95 (Luzerne), 205 at MP 1773.30 (Mercer NJ), Centerville Regulator Station MP 0.11 (Somerset NJ). New York is a delivery area; no pipe is built there. Caution: the 2001 mileposts may not match the later numbering used in the 2014 Leidy Southeast EA (for example Franklin Loop 57.5 to 69.0 on the same line). No towns or coordinates were given.

P8289.notes: Counties crossed: Pittsylvania, Halifax, Charlotte, Mecklenburg, Brunswick (Virginia). The EA calls the new 24-inch pipe SVL B. Seven mainline valves and a new compressor station are named, but no mileposts, towns, roads or coordinates were found. The EA itself (FERC eLibrary CP13-30) was not reachable and no ferc.gov copy was located. The exact mile zero of SVL B was not found. Virginia Southside II (CP15-118) is a separate project.

P8282.notes: CP97-193 is correct. The notices say about 17.77 mi of 16-inch loop on the existing 10-inch Maiden Delivery Lateral in Lincoln and Catawba Counties NC, plus expansion of the Lowesville Meter Station, delivering 38,000 dt/d to Piedmont Natural Gas. Mileposts, the mainline milepost of the tap, and town names were not found. Lowesville is in Lincoln County from general knowledge, not from a source read, so the start is probably Lincoln County and the end Catawba County. No coordinates.
